description: Add a runner build-identity check to `mo update`'s VerifyRuntime stage, behaviorally symmetric to the existing server identity check, comparing the runner's reported buildGitHash against source HEAD and surfacing drift as a non-blocking Warn.

tasks.title: Implement runner build-identity check in VerifyRuntime and wire into the check sequence
tasks.spec: specs/update-runtime-consistency/spec.md#Requirement: Runner build-identity check compares the runner buildGitHash to source HEAD
tasks.description: Add `internal Task<RuntimeCheckResult> CheckRunnerIdentityAsync(UpdateContext, CancellationToken)` to `RuntimeConsistencyValidator.cs`, mirroring `CheckServerIdentityAsync`. It SHALL read `buildGitHash` from `GET /api/runner/identity` via a new private `RunnerIdentitySnapshot` type and `TryGetRunnerIdentityAsync` helper (per design D2/D6), reuse the cached source HEAD from `TryGetSourceHeadAsync(context)` (D5), and resolve to Pass/Warn only — never Fail (D3). Wire it into the `checks` list in `VerifyRuntimeStageAsync` (`MohistCliCommands.Update.Stages.cs`) AFTER `CheckRunnerConnectionAsync` and BEFORE `CheckManagedSkillAssetsAsync`, and update the `--dry-run` line to mention runner identity alongside the other checks. The message text SHALL match the spec exactly: `Runner identity matches source HEAD '<source>'` / `Runner buildGitHash '<runner>' does not match source HEAD '<source>'`. Leave `CheckRunnerConnectionAsync` and its aggregation logic untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: `RuntimeConsistencyValidator.CheckRunnerIdentityAsync` exists and resolves to Pass when runner `buildGitHash` equals source HEAD (message: `Runner identity matches source HEAD '<hash>'`).
The check resolves to Warn (not Fail) when runner `buildGitHash` differs from source HEAD, quoting both hashes in the message.
The check resolves to Warn (not Fail) when the runner reports null/empty `buildGitHash`, and does not block the update.
The check resolves to Warn (not Fail) when source HEAD cannot be determined, and resolves to Warn (not Fail) when `/api/runner/identity` is unreachable.

The check reads `buildGitHash` from `GET /api/runner/identity` and reuses `TryGetSourceHeadAsync(context)` so server and runner identity share one resolved HEAD with no second `git rev-parse` invocation.
`VerifyRuntimeStageAsync` invokes `CheckRunnerIdentityAsync` in the checks list immediately after `CheckRunnerConnectionAsync` and before `CheckManagedSkillAssetsAsync`.
The `--dry-run` output line for VerifyRuntime names runner identity alongside the other component checks.
Existing `CheckRunnerConnectionAsync` active-state check behavior and its Fail-capable aggregation remain unchanged.
The existing aggregation logic (`Any(Fail)` / `Any(Warn)`) correctly derives Ready/Recovered/Failed with the new check present, since it only emits Pass/Warn.

Unit tests in `RuntimeConsistencyValidatorSpecs.cs` cover the match (Pass), mismatch (Warn), missing runner hash (Warn), source HEAD unavailable (Warn), and endpoint unreachable (Warn) scenarios using `RecordingHttpHandler` stubbed on the `/api/runner/identity` absolute path.

Orchestration tests (`UpdateSpecs.cs` or equivalent) that script the full VerifyRuntime sequence include a queued `/api/runner/identity` response and assert the new `[ok|warn] Runner identity:` line appears in order between Runner connection and Managed skill assets.
A `--dry-run` test asserts the dry-run line mentions runner identity.
`npm test` for the CLI (dotnet build with TreatWarningsAsErrors + tests) passes.
tasks.output: Modified `packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/Update/RuntimeConsistencyValidator.cs` (new CheckRunnerIdentityAsync + private RunnerIdentitySnapshot/TryGetRunnerIdentityAsync) and `packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/Update/MohistCliCommands.Update.Stages.cs` (sequence wiring + dry-run message); extended `packages/cli/tests/Mohist.Cli.Tests/RuntimeConsistencyValidatorSpecs.cs` and the VerifyRuntime orchestration test(s); all CLI tests green.
tasks.notes: Design decisions D1–D7 in openspec/changes/issue-275/design.md are authoritative for implementation shape. The change is CLI-only — no server, runner, or API contract changes. Treat the check as additive: removing it returns VerifyRuntime to the prior five-check sequence with no state to clean up.
